question: Can a content-hashed first-party CC0 subset of two source entities and 8 bounded predicates yield an independently verifiable semantic relation carrier, real multi-hop association and exact cold restore without exceeding Wikidata source quotas?
motivation: F27 already consumed one failed source attempt, and its 16MiB cap rejected a larger 14-seed source cohort. This is a distinct frozen smaller DEV source cohort, no rerun or change of F27's frozen budgets.
source: Wikidata Special:EntityData first-party JSON with fixed-revision URI check, content SHA256; source and rights as F27
seed_content_reread: Exact current lastrevid via ?revision=<id>, verify canonical entity JSON SHA; only first-party unqualified nondeprecated Q-P-Q statements
endpoint_order: Bridge endpoints that complete Q42 P31 Q5 P279 * by original source structure first, remaining numeric QID ascending; no hidden outcome data or future-world labels
expected_development_check: If 2-hop exists, source-only numeric graph must agree exactly with same-row symbolic 2-hop and cold snapshot; no assertion of predictive gain. If no admissible associations or no 2-hop in source, classify source/block/no-go, not model learning failure.
negative_controls: missing/invalid English source or property label -> exclude/abstain
wrong revision and changing canonical entity -> block
altered numeric snapshot fails cold canonical validity
shuffled relation composition differs on independent fixture
scope: QTR contributor-only additive source and test files. No native Yggdrasil/Wingless/Hybrid weights edited. No model or donor inference, no paid API, no source first-use, no WSP99 protected data, no schedule, no merges/deploy.
after_source: Seal source relations/bytes and explore a separately frozen direct-weight-programming adapter with equal-information symbolic exact retrieval, disjoint composition/contradiction/retention controls. Do not claim semantic intelligence from graph parity.
